Oral Judgment

This appeal is filed under Section 380 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 to set aside the order dated 17.08.2024 passed by the Principal Judge, Family Court at Bidar [for brevity, 'the Family Court'] on I.A.No.4 filed under Section 340 of Cr.P.C. in Crl.Misc.No.4/2023.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: NC: 2026:KHC-K:856 HC-KAR 2.
The factual matrix of the case is that the marriage of the appellant with respondent No.1 was solemnized on 29.04.2016.
Thereafter, appellant and respondent No.1 lived cordially and they begotten a child i.e., respondent No.2 now aged about 5 years.

Later, due to the alleged harassment meted out by the appellant to respondent No.1, she filed a criminal case against the appellant which was registered in Crime No.48/2022 for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 504 and 506 r/w Section 149 of Indian Penal Code, 1860 [for brevity, 'the IPC'] and Sections 3 and 4 of Rahul vs Soumya And Anr on 3 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198078181/
2 Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.
Subsequently, the respondent No.1 and 2 had filed a petition under Section 125 of Cr.P.C. in Crl.Misc.No.4/2023 before the Family Court.
In the said petition, it is alleged that respondent No.1 had not filed a declaration of assets and liabilities.

Therefore, the appellant filed an application under Section 91 of Cr.P.C. before the Family Court in Crl.Misc.No.4/2023 for directing respondent No.1 to file her affidavit of declaration of NC:
2026:KHC-K:856 HC-KAR assets and liabilities.
The said application was allowed and the Family Court directed respondent No.1 to file a declaration of assets and liabilities.
Accordingly, respondent No.1 filed her declaration of assets and liabilities.

3. It is the case of the appellant - husband that respondent No.1 intentionally suppressed her assets and filed a false affidavit suppressing the true facts with an intention to obtain favourable order of maintenance from the Family Court.

According to the appellant, after ascertaining the affidavit of declaration of assets and liabilities filed by respondent No.1, since the same found to be false, he filed an application under Section 340 of Cr.P.C. for filing false declaration of assets and liabilities and to conduct proceedings against respondent No.1 for the offence punishable under Section 193 of IPC.
The said application came to be rejected by the Family Court.
Hence, this appeal.
NC: 2026:KHC-K:856 HC-KAR 4.
Heard learned counsel for the appellant and learned counsel for respondents so also perused the documents made available before this Court.
5. As could be gathered from records, the relationship between the appellant and the respondents is not in dispute.

On perusal of the impugned order passed by the Family Court, it could be gathered that there is no specific order or finding passed or given by the Family Court in respect of the contents of the affidavit filed by respondent No.1.
Before concluding that there is a falsity in the contents of affidavit, enquiry cannot be conducted for perjury.
The application filed by the appellant under Section 340 of Cr.P.C is totally misconceived and it is filed at premature stage.

6. The Co-ordinate bench of this Court, while passing the order for conducting an enquiry in an application under Section 340 of Cr.P.C. in Criminal Petition No.200700/2024 disposed of on 27.06.2024, NC: 2026:KHC-K:856 HC-KAR observed that if an application is filed under Section 340 of Cr.P.C., preliminary enquiry has to be conducted by the concerned Trial Judge and if the Trial Judge satisfies himself that the allegation of falsity is made out, then only can initiate proceedings.
In the instant case, the appellant has filed the application before such preliminary enquiry by the Family Court on the affidavit filed by respondent No.1.
Hence, at this premature stage the application is not maintainable.
This aspect of the matter has been rightly dealt with by the Family Court.
I find no good ground to interfere with the impugned order.
7. Accordingly, the appeal lacks merits and the same is dismissed.

Sd/-
